title: quercus pubescens subsp. dalechampii
intro: Quercus pubescens subsp. dalechampii, commonly known as Dale's oak, is a subspecies of deciduous tree belonging to the Quercus genus. It has been traditionally used in folk medicine due to its various health benefits, such as antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties, which can help to prevent cell damage, reduce inflammation, and combat infections. The therapeutic actions of Dale's oak include cardiovascular protection, immunomodulation, and antitumor activity, attributed to its bioactive constituents such as flavonoids, phenolic acids, and tannins. Bioactive constituents like quercetin, isorhapontigenin, and 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetic acid in Dale's oak contribute to its medicinal properties.
